instruction: Apply underline formatting to the title text on both the title slide and slide 2

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires applying underline to titles on both slide 1 ('Minimalistic Newsletter') and slide 2 ('Announcement'). Partial credit: 0.5 for slide 1, 0.5 for slide 2.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for slide 1 title underlined, 0.5 for slide 2 title underlined

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements: slide 1 title ('Minimalistic Newsletter') and slide 2 title ('Announcement') are underlined
Getter logic is correct: retrieves PowerPoint file after saving via postconfig (Ctrl+S)
Metric implements proper partial credit scoring: 0.5 per slide
Good edge case handling: recursively extracts text shapes from groups, handles missing slides
Postconfig is appropriate: activates window and saves file before verification

Minor issue: metric checks if ANY run containing the text is underlined (line 46), but doesn't verify ALL runs are underlined. Could give false positive if title text spans multiple runs with mixed formatting. However, this is unlikely in practice since title underline formatting is typically applied to entire shapes.

Minor issue: font.underline check uses truthy test which won't detect inherited underline (when font.underline is None). In practice, explicit formatting should set font.underline to True or an enum value.
Expected values are semantically correct: slide indices (0, 1) match instruction, text values match the actual slide titles
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking that ALL runs containing parts of the target text are underlined, not just ANY run, to avoid false positives when text spans multiple runs with inconsistent formatting
Consider explicitly checking for font.underline == True or checking if font.underline is a specific MSO_UNDERLINE enum value, rather than relying on truthy check
Consider logging a warning when the target text is not found in the slide, to help debug verification failures
